title: Playwright Hybrid Framework Schema
description: Scenario file structure for the Playwright Hybrid Keyword-Driven Framework.

config.description: Configuration that applies to this scenario file only.

locatorFile.description: Locator file in data/locators/ used by this suite (e.g. swag-lab.json).

tags.description: Tags applied to every test case in this suite (e.g. ["@saucedemo", "@ci"]). Each tag is appended to the generated test title, so Playwright's --grep can select it.

status.description: Suite lifecycle status. Default "ready": every locator must be resolved or npm run validate fails. Set "wip" while a generated suite is still waiting on the codegen locator handoff - unresolved TODO_LOCATOR stubs are then reported as outstanding work instead of failing the build, and the runner marks the suite's tests fixme and tags them @wip. Everything else stays strict. Set it back to "ready" once the stubs are resolved.

enableAutoHealing.description: Opt this suite into optional runtime locator healing. Default false. Requires OPENAI_API_KEY; skipped with a warning if unset. A heal applies to the current run only and is recorded in test-results/heal-report.json - locator files are never modified during a run.

storageState.description: Path to a saved authenticated session/storage state file (e.g. .auth/user.json).

scenario.description: Test suite name, shown in the report.

testId.description: Test case identifier, format TC_[FEATURE]_[NN] (e.g. TC_LOGIN_01).

description.description: Optional longer description of what this test case verifies.

tags.description: Tags for this test case only, merged with the suite-level config.tags and appended to the generated test title.

dataTable.description: Data-driven rows. Each object produces one generated test case; reference row keys as {{key}} in steps.

preconditions.description: Setup steps, executed before the main flow.

postconditions.description: Teardown steps, always executed even when the test fails.

action.description: Action keyword. Full catalog with required fields: docs/ACTIONS.md.

page.description: Page key in the locator file, PascalCase (e.g. LoginPage).

element.description: Element key within the page, camelCase (e.g. usernameInput).

data.description: Input value or expected value, depending on the action. Supports {{...}} tokens.

variable.description: Runtime variable name to store a captured value into (used by store_text).

storeAs.description: Runtime variable name to store the value just entered (optional, used by fill).

url.description: URL, used by the API actions, mock_route, unmock_route, and goto.

key.description: Key to press (used by press_key, e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape).

attribute.description: HTML attribute name to assert on (used by verify_attribute).

count.description: Expected number of matching elements (used by verify_element_count).

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Used by wait, and by wait_for_element (default 10000).

state.description: Target element state for wait_for_element. Default visible.

flow.description: Sub-flow file name in data/flows/ (used by call_flow).

params.description: Parameters passed into the sub-flow (used by call_flow).

status.description: HTTP status code for the mocked response. mock_route only - it does not assert anything. To assert the status of a real API response, use "expected_status".

contentType.description: Content-Type of the mocked response. Default application/json.

snapshotName.description: Baseline image file name to compare against (used by verify_visual_snapshot).

maxDiffPixelRatio.description: Maximum allowed pixel difference ratio, 0 to 1. Default 0.05.

headers.description: HTTP headers for API requests (e.g. Authorization).

store_response.description: Extract a value from the API response into a runtime variable.

key.description: Key to read from the JSON response body.

variable.description: Runtime variable name to store the extracted value in.

expected_status.description: Exact HTTP status an API response must have (api_get / api_post / api_put / api_patch / api_delete). When set, the status must match exactly, which is what makes a negative API test expressible. When omitted, any 2xx or 3xx passes. Not read by mock_route - use "status" for a mocked response status.
